title: GuardDecision
description: One decision of the Trooth guard (trooth/guard, docs/GUARD.md): allow, hold for a person, or deny an ACTION the customer's agent is about to take, under the customer's policy, with reason codes. It is made on the customer's machine and is never a statement about whether a company is safe. The contract is the one in section 8 of the Trooth Network brief; reasons may also carry a detail string. `trooth guard decide --json` prints this document when the policy covers the tool, and a GuardNotCovered ($defs/notCovered) when it does not; schemas/guard-decide-output.v1.schema.json accepts either.

decision.description: allow: every required check held and every rule passed. hold: route the action to a person. deny: a proof failed or a rule the customer marked absolute failed (or the customer's policy chose deny for no record or no source).

reasons.description: Why, one entry per check or rule. An allow carries only RULE_PASSED.

subject.description: Exact entity ID checked, e.g. trooth:domain:acme.com. Empty when the action named no host.

policy.description: The policy the decision was made under.

evidence.description: The signed, logged facts the rules read.

action.description: The intercepted tool call: name, target host, amount or data class. Stored locally, never sent to Trooth.

notCovered.title: GuardNotCovered
notCovered.description: What `trooth guard decide --json` prints when the policy does not cover the tool: nothing was decided, nothing was read, and the command exits 0. It is not an allow and carries no decision; the caller lets the call run as its own controls intend.

covered.description: Always false: the policy's applies_to.tools does not match the tool.

policy.description: The policy that does not cover the tool.

note.description: A plain sentence saying that nothing was decided.

reason.title: GuardReason
reason.description: One reason code, with what it is about.

fact_id.description: Stable ID of the fact this reason is about

rule_id.description: The customer's rule that produced this reason

needed.description: For EVIDENCE_MISSING: the claim type that would satisfy the rule

detail.description: A plain sentence on what was found. Written by the guard, never copied from vendor content.

policyRef.title: GuardPolicyRef
policyRef.description: Which policy, by id, version and the SHA-256 of its RFC 8785 canonical JSON.

sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the policy as parsed.

evidence.title: GuardEvidence
evidence.description: One signed, logged fact a rule read.

fact_id.description: trooth:statement:<sha256>#<claim>: the statement and the claim read from it.

statement_sha256.description: SHA-256 (hex) of the statement's exact payload bytes.

log_index.description: The statement's entry in Trooth's log, or null when it is not shown in the log.

stale_after.description: When the fact stops being fresh for this rule (the rule's max_age_days, else the evidence class's stale-after), or null when unknown.
